---
# Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
# Licensed under the MIT License.

name: Update CI Dependencies

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows:
      - Release – Initiate
    types:
      - completed
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch: null

if: >-
  github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
  (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
  (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
  github.event.workflow_run.event == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
  github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository))

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  copilot-requests: write
  pull-requests: read

concurrency:
  group: update-ci-dependencies
  cancel-in-progress: false

engine: copilot

network:
  allowed:
    - defaults
    - github
    - learn.microsoft.com

tools:
  edit:
  bash:
    - git *
    - gh api *
    - gh pr list *
    - gh pr view *
    - gh actions-lock
    - gh actions-lock *
    - jq *
    - curl *

checkout:
  github-token: ${{ github.token }}
  fetch:
    - "*"
  fetch-depth: 0

# PR preparation and publishing share a token reference, not a credential.
# The agent gets the native read token; only safe_outputs mints a write token.
pre-steps:
  - name: Configure Read-Only Repository Token
    id: repository-token
    run: printf 'token=%s\n' "$GH_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

steps:
  - name: Install Workflow Lockfile Tool
    run: gh extension install github/gh-actions-lock --pin v0.4.0
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

safe-outputs:
  environment: production
  push-to-pull-request-branch:
    target: "*"
    required-labels:
      - release
    max: 1
    if-no-changes: ignore
    protected-files: allowed
    allowed-files:
      - .github/workflows/build.yml
      - .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml
      - .github/workflows/release-initiate.yml
      - .github/workflows/release-publish.yml
      - .github/workflows/actions.lock
      - .github/actions/mint-github-app-token/action.yml
      - .azure-devops/*.yml
      - package.json
      - .nvmrc
    github-token: ${{ steps.repository-token.outputs.token }}
  noop:
    report-as-issue: false

jobs:
  safe_outputs:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    pre-steps:
      - name: App Token – Mint
        id: repository-token
        uses: microsoft/PR-Metrics/.github/actions/mint-github-app-token@5fe360db472f2604e1d2c0f5d33600d033db40ae
        with:
          azure-client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          azure-tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          azure-subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
          permissions: '{"contents":"write","pull_requests":"write","workflows":"write"}'
---

# Update CI Dependencies

Refresh CI dependency pins on the existing release pull request after
`Release – Initiate` has finished its npm dependency updates. Do not create a
branch or a pull request.

## Select the Release Pull Request

Use the GitHub CLI to find open pull requests in `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY` that:

- Target `main` and have the `release` label.
- Have their head branch in this repository, not a fork.
- Have a branch matching `release/vX.Y.Z`.
- Have `[Autogenerated] Release v` somewhere in the title. PR Metrics can
  prepend size and coverage indicators, so do not require a title prefix.

There must be exactly one matching pull request. If there are none or more than
one, make no changes and report the reason with the `noop` safe output.

Fetch and check out the latest head of that release branch. Use repository
files as data; do not execute scripts, actions, or package lifecycle hooks from
the release branch.

## Scope

Edit only these files:

- `.github/workflows/build.yml`
- `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-initiate.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-publish.yml`
- `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, using its generator
- `.github/actions/mint-github-app-token/action.yml`
- `.azure-devops/*.yml`
- `package.json`, only to correct an inconsistent `engines.node` value
- `.nvmrc`, if present

Do not edit this workflow, its generated `.lock.yml`, application code, npm
dependencies, `package-lock.json`, or `dist`.

## GitHub Action Pins

Inspect all actions in the permitted workflow and composite-action YAML files.
For each external action, resolve the latest stable release and its tag's commit
SHA. Update the 40-character SHA and the trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment together.
Subpaths of one action repository, such as `github/codeql-action/init` and
`github/codeql-action/analyze`, must use the same release and SHA.

```bash
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest --jq '.tag_name'
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs/tags/<tag> --jq '.object'
```

`releases/latest` can return a tag that is not an action version. For example,
CodeQL also publishes `codeql-bundle-*` releases. If necessary, list releases and
select the newest stable `vX.Y.Z` action release:

```bash
gh api 'repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases?per_page=100' --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.draft == false and .prerelease == false) | .tag_name | select(test("^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$"))'
```

If a tag refers to an annotated tag object, dereference it through the Git tags
API until you reach a commit. Never use a tag-object SHA as an action pin.

Preserve `$/` references to this repository's actions. Do not replace them with
`./` references or change the trusted signing action's implementation. Leave
deliberately moving 1ES template `release` references unchanged.

Check open Dependabot pull requests before making an action update. If an open
pull request already covers that update, skip the duplicate and report it. Do
not merge or change another pull request.

## Azure DevOps Task Versions

In `.azure-devops/*.yml`, tasks use major versions such as `Npm@1`, `UseNode@1`,
and `EsrpCodeSigning@6`. For built-in tasks, check the `Tasks/` directories in
[`microsoft/azure-pipelines-tasks`][ado-tasks-repo] and the
[Azure Pipelines task reference][ado-tasks]. An `AzureCLIV3` directory confirms
that major version 3 exists.

Review release notes and required inputs before changing a task major version.
Add newly required inputs and replace deprecated or renamed inputs. Use the
input names in the reference documentation's YAML syntax; do not replace a
supported name with an alias. For example, `AzureCLI@3` requires
`connectionType: azureRM` and still documents `azureSubscription`.

Leave internal-extension tasks unchanged unless their release notes are
available. These include `EsrpCodeSigning`, `PoliCheck`,
`PublishSecurityAnalysisLogs`, `PostAnalysis`, and
`ComponentGovernanceComponentDetection`. Never update this product's own
`PRMetrics@N` task as part of this refresh.

## Node.js Runtime Consistency

Do not upgrade the Node.js runtime. Check that the existing intended pin agrees
across:

- `actions/setup-node` inputs in the permitted workflows.
- `UseNode` inputs in `.azure-devops/*.yml`.
- `package.json`'s `engines.node`, preserving its comparison operator.
- `.nvmrc`, if present.

If these values differ, use Git history to identify the most recent deliberate
runtime change and align only the divergent values. Updating the `UseNode` task
major does not authorize changing its Node.js version input. Do not change
compiler-managed runtimes in the generated agentic workflow.

## Regenerate the Actions Lockfile

After updating action references, regenerate the native GitHub Actions
dependency lockfile, including transitive dependencies:

```bash
gh actions-lock --no-narrow --no-interactive
gh actions-lock --verify
```

Keep the generated `.github/workflows/actions.lock` in the same change as the
action updates. Do not edit it by hand. Do not regenerate the agentic workflow's
separate `update-ci-dependencies.lock.yml` during a dependency refresh.

## Publish the Changes

Preserve formatting, trailing newlines, and unrelated changes. Before
publishing, fetch the remote release branch again. Build automation can add
generated commits while you work. Integrate its latest head without discarding
those commits, and regenerate the Actions lockfile if the action inputs changed.
Never force-push.

Use `push_to_pull_request_branch` to publish only the scoped changes to the
selected release pull request, with commit message `chore: refresh CI pins`.
Do not push directly or call write APIs. The trusted safe-output job signs and
publishes the commit with the repository's App token, so Build runs on the new
commit. If no updates are needed, report that through `noop`.

[ado-tasks]: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/
[ado-tasks-repo]: https://github.com/microsoft/azure-pipelines-tasks
